title: Concrete security features versus third-party seals and privacy statements
statement:
Consumers in an experimental e-commerce study valued concrete security features more than third-party privacy/security seals or privacy statements, so a seal can be treated as supporting evidence rather than the only visible answer to a security objection. (ScienceDirect)

Options:
- Concrete security details: security-feature-explanation (fits: high risk, financial, privacy sensitive)
- Security seal: third-party-security-seal (fits: supporting cue, compliance led, compact)
- Privacy summary: privacy-policy-summary (fits: data sensitive, transparent, low clutter)
- Layered trust block: layered-trust-panel (fits: high consideration, evidence led, dense information)
appliesWhen: Applies to: ecommerce, online retail, online payments, privacy sensitive sites. Audience: adults, general.

source.title: Trustworthiness in electronic commerce: the role of privacy, security, and site attributes
source.authors: France Bélanger; Janine S. Hiller; Wanda J. Smith
source.venue: The Journal of Strategic Information Systems
